there is a barrier effect between the tandem genes RASSF1 and BLU in the 3 p21.3 region, and that this barrier effect is provided by the CTC binding to the insulators between these tandem genes.
CTCF bound to the insulator between BLU and RASFF1A genes in normal cells provides a barrier activity to separate the distinct epigenetic domain of these two tandem head-to-head genes.
CTCF insulator separates the distinct epigenetic boundaries for BLU and Rassf1a loci.

the epigenetic regulation of two adjacent TSGs in the same chromosomal region.
the mechanism of gene regulation in the 3 p21.3 region and the role that epigenetic changes play in cancer.

there are two distinct epigenetic barriers separated by a CTCP binding domain between RASSFIA and BLU genes.
there are two distinct epigenetic boundaries separated by the insulator of RASSF/BLU genes.

there are two distinct transcriptionally important CpGs in the 3' region of RASSFIA and BLU genes and the CTCF bound insulator located between the two genes provides barrier activity in the separate domains.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CTCF is a key player in the maintenance of epigenetic domains for RASSFIA and BLU in the context of the 3p gene cluster.
the insulator between RASSFIA and BLU is a barrier for the epigenetic spread from the promoter of BLU to RASSFIA.
the CTCF bound insulator between RASSFIA and BLU genes provides a barrier effect for the separate epigenetic states of the juxtaposed RASSF1 and BLU loci.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the barrier function of CTCF is lost in cancer cells, and this may be one of the reasons for the frequent co-silencing of these two TSGs in human lung cancer cells.
the insulator sequences between the tandem genes, RASSF1 and BLU, may play a role in maintaining the distinct epigenetic states of these two genes.
the insulator between BLU and RASSF1A genes is an important epigenetic barrier to prevent the spread of epigenetic modifications from one locus to another.
